data: My family taught me to leave enough fish for next season, and our village depends on us doing that. With 100 tons in the lake, we can each catch 10 tons this month, leave 50, and let it double back to 100. That’s $10,000 apiece each month for as long as we stick to it. I propose we agree to that equal limit and review everyone’s catches together afterward. John, would you be willing to commit to 10 tons?

I’m in for 10 tons. My family’s livelihood has always depended on keeping this lake healthy, and I want our village to have that same security. Let’s make 10 tons each a firm ceiling, not just a target, and check the lake’s stock together each month before setting our limits. John, can we count on you to join us?

Thanks, Emma—you can count on me to keep to that ceiling. If the lake starts a future month below 100 tons, we should lower our catches together so at least half the stock remains to reproduce. John, what do you think—can you commit to 10 tons this month?
Kate and Jack, are you both willing to keep to 10 tons this month too? An agreement needs all five of us, and I’d like to hear any concerns before we head out.
